decisions.reason: The low-noise burner builds directly on the firm's existing infrared heating and combustion know-how, so management is likely to retain it as an improvable differentiating module despite limited public visibility after launch.
A gas infrared plaque heater is very close to the firm's core knowledge base and its dedicated product page suggests enough initial commitment and market feedback to justify keeping it.
The luminous radiant heater fits the firm's established gas-infrared competence, but its lower prominence makes it somewhat more exposed if early results were only moderate.
The gas-fired infrared tube heater is technologically well within the firm's absorptive capacity, though overlap with another tube-heater launch raises some risk of later portfolio rationalisation.
As a standard gas infrared plaque heater with its own page, it appears closely aligned with the firm's established product family and likely to be kept as a core offering.
Although it is related to the firm's existing know-how, it looks redundant with product D and is the most likely candidate to be removed if management consolidates similar tube-heater variants.
